title: Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club holds free fishing clinic for kids - NewsBreak
text:
By Travis Chinn Maren Ewertz No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
SPIRIT LAKE , Iowa ( KCAU ) — Over 100 kids gathered at Memorial Park in Spirit Lake on Wednesday night for the Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club’s kids’ free fishing clinic.
“Our main focus here at the Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club is to make sure that we introduce kids to the outdoors and fishing, as well as conservation. It’s something that a lot of us take for granted. And we know there are several kids here tonight and that have come to our events, and it’s the first time they’ve cast a pole or the first time they’ve reeled in a fish,” said Nathan Albrecht, Board Member for the Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club.
Story continues below
The club set up three different stations to teach the kids about different areas of fishing.
“We hope to teach the kids about water safety, a little fish cleaning demonstration, as well as some fish identification, so the DNR is out shocking some fish right now for the kids to look at,” added Albrecht.
After the kids go through each station, it’s time for a fishing contest where the young anglers can win some prizes.
“We have a big fish category, so out here in the lake, you can catch multiple different species, so every species we’re going to give away two gift cards, one to the top two biggest fish caught in each category,” said Albrecht.
Along with acquiring knowledge, each kid who attended the clinic went home with a new rod and reel, courtesy of the Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club.
If you missed Wednesday’s event, don’t worry, because the Iowa Great Lakes Fishing Club is holding another free kids fishing clinic on April 29 at Stolley’s Pond in Spencer .
